conflicts.permit: Lark allows third party vendors to use cookies and other technologies to collect information when you visit our Sites for the purpose of serving you tailored or targeted advertising
conflicts.prohibit: Lark does not disclose Personal Data to third parties for their direct marketing purposes.
conflicts.situation: A visitor browses Lark's site while a network advertiser's cookies collect the visitor's identifiers to serve that advertiser network's targeted ads on other websites.
conflicts.reason: The policy lets ad vendors collect cookie data, which it defines as Personal Data, for targeted ads, yet denies disclosure for third parties' direct marketing. It does not say whether network advertising counts.

conflicts.permit: In our applications we may ask you to submit and we may process other non-personally identifiable information that may be private to you such as your age range, year of birth and gender, provided that year of birth and gender are collected solely for users who identify themselves in our apps as above the age of 13.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not collect any user provided information, but we may collect certain information automatically
conflicts.situation: A user over 13 enters their year of birth and gender when one of the apps asks for them.
conflicts.reason: One statement says the company collects no user-provided information. Another says the apps ask users to submit age range, birth year and gender. No exception reconciles the two.

conflicts.permit: Advertisers and advertising networks use some of the information collected by the our services, including, but not limited to, the unique identification ID of your mobile device and your mobile telephone number.
conflicts.prohibit: BestRingtonesApps collects only anonymous information for the purposes of targeted advertising and tracking of user behavior within the game.
conflicts.situation: The app collects a user's device ID and mobile phone number, and advertising networks use them to serve targeted ads.
conflicts.reason: A phone number and device ID identify a user, yet the policy says only anonymous information is collected for targeted advertising. The encryption remark does not say which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: For users who identify themselves as above the age of 13 and have not opted out from behavioral advertising, we may use such information to display targeted ads.
conflicts.prohibit: As a responsible company, we do not use automatic decision-making or profiling.
conflicts.situation: A user over 13 who has not opted out sees ads targeted using the age and gender they entered and their in-app behavior.
conflicts.reason: Targeting ads on age, gender and tracked behavior fits the GDPR sense of profiling that the policy invokes. The policy denies profiling and does not define a narrower meaning.

conflicts.permit: Some apps contain the option to contact us or register via mail.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not collect any personal information about the users of our apps.
conflicts.situation: An app user registers by email inside an app, and the company keeps the address and later sends product news to it.
conflicts.reason: An email address from an app user is personal information. The policy denies collecting any personal information about app users and gives no exception for contact details users submit.

conflicts.permit: We collect this Information to get better performance and reliability of our Games and to get a better perceptive of what users in general have a preference.
conflicts.prohibit: In our apps & games we do not collect, store, or share any personal information or location data.
conflicts.situation: A user plays a game that uses Google Analytics, which records the user's country and city for the developer.
conflicts.reason: The policy says it collects the Google Analytics information, which includes country and city. It also says its apps collect no location data, with no exception for coarse location.

conflicts.permit: Some of our apps and games might use Google Analytics (third party scripts) that collect the following information
conflicts.prohibit: We do not share, sell or in any other way give other persons or companies.
conflicts.situation: Google Analytics scripts in a game send the user's device, city and behavior data to Google.
conflicts.reason: Using third-party scripts gives the data to Google, another company, while the policy says the information is not given to other persons or companies. The policy does not say which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: We may share your personal information for any sweepstakes or promotions you enter in connection with the Services in order to administer, market, sponsor or fulfill such sweepstakes or promotions as necessary
conflicts.prohibit: We do not share your personal information with third parties for the purpose of direct marketing.
conflicts.situation: A California user enters a promotion, and the company shares the entry details with a third party to market the promotion.
conflicts.reason: The sweepstakes clause allows sharing personal information to market promotions. The California section denies sharing with third parties for direct marketing. The policy states no carve-out for promotions.

conflicts.permit: providing the data to our group companies, ad agencies and ad platforms to target advertisements of BNEA (and its group company) games and services to you outside of this service
conflicts.prohibit: BNEA has not “sold” or “shared” Personal Data for purposes of California Privacy Laws.
conflicts.situation: A California user consents to targeted advertising, and BNEA gives the user's data to ad platforms to target BNEA ads outside the app.
conflicts.reason: California law treats disclosure to ad platforms for cross-context targeted advertising as sharing. The policy describes this disclosure but states it has not shared Personal Data, without explaining the difference.
